title: Fix Historical Gross/Net parity lineage hash validation
author: agent:/root

scope.goal: Make the deployed incremental Historical Gross/Net parity workflow accept a lineage binding that it prepared itself, so eligible historical Paper targets can reach their existing accounting transaction instead of all being deferred on a deterministic hash mismatch.
inScope: Use one canonical JSON byte representation when HistoricalGrossNetParityPaperPreparer produces LineagePayloadJson/LineageHash and when storage validates that same pair.
Add a focused regression for lineage JSON containing UTC offsets and nested canonical fill JSON, including the plus-sign escaping difference observed in production.
Build and focused-test verification of the correction.
outOfScope: Changing Fee, Gross, Net, ROI, donor, sorting, cutoff, candidate paging, ownership, Live balance, or VenueReported behavior.
Changing PostgreSQL schema or production data; deploying or restarting the service.
Adding a new logging framework or changing unrelated parity diagnostics, documentation, or historical rows.
scope.periodOrFilter: Historical Gross/Net parity targets originated before 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z; the code correction itself applies to every Paper lineage payload prepared by the incremental workflow.
scope.firstVerification: Compare the producer and validator hash inputs against one fresh production candidate page in a server-enforced read-only transaction and prove the exact mismatch before editing.

requirements.text: Correct the lineage binding contract so preparation stores the canonical normalized lineage JSON and its SHA-256, which the existing mutation validator reproduces exactly.
acceptanceCriteria: For a prepared Paper target, SHA-256(LineagePayloadJson encoded as UTF-8) equals LineageHash and remains equal after the validator's JSON normalization step.
A production-shaped lineage payload containing a DateTimeOffset with +00:00 and nested fill JSON no longer changes hash when preparation hands it to validation.
The correction changes no accounting number, target eligibility, donor choice, target order, cutoff, or database field.

verification.command: Inspect the focused diff and producer/validator hash call sites.
verification.expected: The producer canonicalizes LineagePayloadJson before hashing/storing it, while the existing storage validator remains unchanged and reproduces the same bytes.
verification.evidence: Focused inspection confirmed the preparer normalizes lineage JSON with JsonDocument.Parse plus JsonSerializer.Serialize, hashes and stores that canonical payload, while the storage validator remains unchanged and uses the identical normalization.

verification.expected: Focused processor tests pass, including the canonical lineage regression.
verification.evidence: PaperFakFeeBackfillProcessorTests passed 34/34 from the marked D:\CodexTemp run.

verification.command: dotnet build PolyCopyTrader.sln -c Debug --no-restore --artifacts-path <marked D:\CodexTemp run artifacts path>
verification.expected: Solution build exits 0; warnings are reported exactly.
verification.evidence: PolyCopyTrader.sln build exited 0 with 0 errors and 126 pre-existing warnings.

requirements.text: Add a regression test that fails with the deployed raw-versus-normalized lineage hash behavior and passes only when both sides use the same canonical representation.
acceptanceCriteria: The test fixture includes the observed escaping boundary rather than only JSON without timezone offsets.
The test asserts both the stored payload/hash pair and validator-style normalization equality.
No production database connection is required by the regression test.

verification.command: Run the focused lineage regression directly by its fully qualified test name.
verification.expected: The regression exits 0 and proves canonical hash reproduction.
verification.evidence: HistoricalParityPaperPrepare_CanonicalizesTimezoneBearingLineageBeforeHashing passed 1/1 and asserted canonical payload/hash equality plus the observed \u002B03:00 escaping boundary.

verification.expected: No whitespace error is reported in the two governed files.
verification.evidence: git diff --check reported no whitespace errors in the two governed files; only line-ending conversion warnings were emitted.
